check.name: UnnecessaryPermitsClause
check.description:
Checks that a permits clause of a sealed class or interface is not unnecessary, i.e. that it is not possible to omit the clause and have the compiler infer the exact same set of permitted subtypes.

See the Java Language Specification for more information about sealed classes.

This Check does not perform full type resolution. A permitted type is treated as local to the file only when the name in the permits clause can actually refer to a type declared in the same compilation unit: an unqualified name must denote a type declared in the compilation unit, a member type of the sealed type, or a member type of one of its enclosing types, and a qualified name must match the nesting path of a type declared in the compilation unit. An unrelated type that merely shares a simple name with the permitted type is therefore not mistaken for it.
